items.text: Even if we don't know the names of the psalmists, reading the Psalms allows us to feel as if we know their hearts. These ancient words offer a window into the souls of God's people, expressing their feelings about God, their worries, and how they found peace, resonating with believers across generations.

items.text: The Psalms acknowledge that fear, sorrow, and anxiety are normal human experiences, even for those with faith. However, their power lies in offering inspiring solutions, primarily through complete trust in the Lord. By focusing on His attributes and the peace He provides, we can find strength.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: In Psalm 23, imagery like 'green pastures' and 'still waters' symbolizes the Lord’s tender care and guidance. The comforting 'rod' and 'staff' represent His protection and discipline, while a 'cup' that runs over signifies His abundant blessings and eternal provision for those who follow Him.

Several Psalms foretold aspects of Jesus Christ's mortal life. New Testament Christians recognized these connections, seeing prophecies fulfilled in His ministry and atoning sacrifice. Studying these links deepens our understanding of His divine mission and the promises He makes to us.

items.text: The created world powerfully declares the glory of God. As we observe the earth and the heavens, we can feel inspired by the Lord’s magnificent creations. Singing hymns that reflect on His handiwork can enhance our appreciation for His goodness and divine power.

The Lord is our shepherd, guiding us through life's journey. He leads us to places of rest and refreshment, and His rod and staff protect us from danger. We can find solace and assurance in His constant care, knowing He will lead us home.

When we face adversity, the Psalms remind us that the Lord is our refuge and strength. He is a present help in times of trouble, a mighty fortress against our enemies. Even when the earth shakes, we can find peace and security in Him.

The righteous are blessed because they delight in the law of the Lord and meditate on His word day and night. They are like trees planted by rivers of water, bringing forth fruit in their season. Their prosperity is assured, and their endeavors succeed.

The Lord’s loving-kindness is better than life itself, so our lips will praise Him. We will bless Him as long as we live, lifting our hands in His name. Our souls will feast on rich fare, and our mouths will praise Him with joyful lips.

The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament shows His handiwork. Day unto day they utter speech, and night unto night they reveal knowledge. There is no speech or language where their voice is not heard.
